capture.final_message:
Treat the two equivalences as packaging: prove all four sides independently using standard finiteness invariance.

- Interpret `Set.bind s f` as the indexed union
  \[
  \{b \mid \exists a\in s,\ b\in f(a)\}.
  \]
  A finite index set with finite fibers has finite union/bind. `Set.pure a` is simply the singleton `{a}`, hence finite.

- For `[Finite (Set.Elem s)]`, use the subtype inclusion `Set.Elem s → α`; its range is exactly `s`. The range of a finite type is finite.

- An equivalence `α ≃ β` transports finiteness in both directions. Taking the negation of finiteness—or directly using invariance of `Infinite` under equivalence—gives `Infinite α ↔ Infinite β`.

After establishing these facts, form each `Iff` from the independently true sides and combine them with `And`. The main mechanism throughout is representing sets as finite images/indexed unions and transporting finiteness along functions or equivalences.
